section_summary: Pages 426–484 conclude a report on Japanese political movements, with histories of labor and farmers’ unions, a roster of Communist Party committees, election tables, charts, an index, and a distribution list. The remaining pages contain 1947 diplomatic reporting on Soviet and Chinese commentary about Japan, a proposed British parliamentary visit, British reaction to remarks attributed to Prime Minister Katayama, and a covering despatch for a report on Japan’s April elections.

subfiles.title: Report on Japanese ideological and political movements, appendices and index
subfiles.about: The concluding portion of a report surveys political labor and agrarian organizations and Communist Party leadership.
subfiles.summary: This portion finishes histories of labor unions and farmers’ unions, including their splits, political affiliations, wartime suppression, and postwar revival. It then lists Communist Party committee members from 1922 to 1937, charts proletarian election results and organizational lineages, and supplies a personal and organizational index plus a distribution list.

subfiles.title: Moscow telegram on Izvestia criticism of Ashida
subfiles.about: Reports Soviet criticism of Ashida’s suggestions on the Kuril Islands and Japanese armed forces.
subfiles.summary: Izvestia calls Ashida’s views evidence of revived Japanese militarism and criticizes occupation policy.

subfiles.title: London airgram on a proposed British parliamentary mission to Japan
subfiles.about: Describes plans for a five-member House of Commons mission to investigate conditions in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Office expects a parliamentary visit during the August recess, possibly including G. Lang and John Paton. The sender recommends welcoming it to improve British parliamentary and public understanding of Japan.

subfiles.title: Moscow airgram on Red Fleet commentary about Japan
subfiles.about: Summarizes a Soviet newspaper article alleging sabotage, economic disorder, and plans to regain the Kuriles.
subfiles.summary: Red Fleet blames Japanese business, recent governments, and occupation authorities for economic disorder.

subfiles.title: Changchun telegram on Chinese editorials concerning Japan
subfiles.about: Reports two Chinese editorials warning of renewed Japanese imperialism and criticizing U.S. occupation policy.
subfiles.summary: The editorials urge Japan to learn from its past and China to rely on itself.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement sheet for London airgram
subfiles.about: Designates the attached white copy as the record copy because the yellow action copy was not returned.
subfiles.summary: Directs return of the replacement copy to Central Records.

subfiles.title: London airgram on British reaction to Katayama interview
subfiles.about: Reports British press accounts of remarks attributed to Prime Minister Katayama comparing Japan’s recovery with British austerity.
subfiles.summary: The Manchester Guardian and The Times describe British official indignation over an interview published in Stars and Stripes. Katayama denies the comparison. The embassy consults the Foreign Office, which says Gascoigne may raise the matter with MacArthur.

subfiles.title: Moscow telegram on Red Star commentary about reaction in Japan
subfiles.about: Summarizes Soviet allegations that Japanese conservatives and business interests are weakening democratization.
subfiles.summary: Red Star criticizes occupation authorities, the Katayama government, and proposed changes to workers’ organizations.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of report on the Japanese elections of April 1947
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits five copies of a Government Section report on Japan’s April 1947 elections.
subfiles.summary: Explains that the June 20 report was unavailable for earlier transmission.

subfiles.title: The Japanese Elections, April 1947
subfiles.from: Government Section, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Introduces an official report on the conduct and results of Japan’s April 1947 elections.
subfiles.summary: The title and contents pages list chapters on democratic safeguards, publicity, campaign issues, local and national elections, and women voters. The introduction outline identifies the new legislative houses, first popular local executive and assembly elections, timing, public interest, election law, and election procedures.
